metadata.title: Assessing Scientific, Reading and Mathematical Literacy: A Framework for PISA 2006

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD framework describes the PISA 2006 assessment design rather than estimating model-based effects from a released micro-dataset. PISA uses nationally representative samples of 15-year-old students and a rotated test design with multiple booklets, so analysts working with PISA microdata should apply the complex survey sampling weights provided in the international database to obtain population-representative estimates. The framework does not specify replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) or the exact weight variable names, so those should be taken from the PISA Data Explorer/Data User Guide for the specific cycle. Because this document is a conceptual assessment framework, it does not report any PV estimation or missing-data strategy; therefore, weighting guidance is limited to how PISA is designed to support valid inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a framework describing how PISA 2006 constructs and reports literacy scales (science, reading, mathematics) rather than an empirical analysis predicting student outcomes. As such, it does not implement PV-based achievement modeling or report any missing-data handling procedure for an analytic model. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the extraction because there is no student-level estimation pipeline in this text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used to describe PISA 2006 design: paper-and-pencil tests administered to nationally representative samples of 15-year-old students in participating countries; each student receives a subset of items via a rotated test design across 13 linked testing booklets. The framework states that typically between 5 000 and 10 000 students per country are tested and that at least 150 schools are involved, but it does not define an analytic subsample with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for a specific empirical analysis.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD framework specifies the conceptual and measurement design for PISA 2006, with scientific literacy as the major domain and reading and mathematical literacy as additional domains. It describes paper-and-pencil administration (two hours total), stimulus-based units, and a rotated test design in 13 booklets where different students take different combinations of items, enabling coverage of a broad item pool. For science, it details three scientific competencies (identify issues, explain phenomena scientifically, use evidence) and knowledge categories (knowledge of science and knowledge about science), plus an innovative embedded attitudinal component assessed in-context. For reading, it defines reading literacy as understanding/using/reflecting on written texts, distinguishes continuous vs non-continuous formats, and specifies five processes that are reported via composite and subscales. The framework also explains how PISA reports outcomes on proficiency scales (e.g., mean 500, SD 100) using IRT-based scaling and proficiency levels for major domains, while noting that minor domains may be reported without levels.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical assessment framework document: it does not report an analytic sample, model estimation, or predictive performance metrics. Consequently, fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, PV handling implementation details, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not populated because no empirical ML pipeline is executed in the text. The document’s value is in specifying constructs, item organization, scoring approaches (including partial credit), and reporting scales that later PISA cycles use for valid cross-national measurement.
